title: Landing Party — Upgrade Options
summary: Commander Spock pays off land names: whenever he enters or attacks he reveals the top card, lets you cast it for free if its mana value is at most the number of differently named lands you control, puts it onto the battlefield if it's a land, and otherwise draws it. The stock list ramps, lands 35 different names and already carries six blink and copy effects that make Spock enter again (Chief Kyle, Temporal Tribulation, The Guardian of Forever, Balance of Terror, Colossal Clone Master, Shore Leave Planet), but it has only three real answers and fires its ten landfall payoffs off a single extra land drop. Each direction buys four shared answers plus one engine of six cards, and every direction keeps the blink pieces the precon built around Spock.

notes: Curve is high: 59 nonland cards besides Spock at an average MV of 3.58, with ten at six mana or more (eight at six, Lt. Arex at seven, Planet Killer at eight).

Spock's free-cast ceiling is the number of differently named lands on the battlefield — 35 names across 40 lands, but 4 Forest, 2 Island and 2 Plains mean those 40 cards only ever count as 35, and the ceiling creeps up one name at a time.
Only three cards answer a resolved creature (Path to Exile, Reality Shift, Beast Within), and those same three are the deck's entire instant-speed interaction.

Sixteen lands enter tapped (thirteen outright, plus three fetch lands that bring one in tapped), and three more — Mutavault, Reliquary Tower, Temple of the False God — are colourless in a three-colour deck. Shore Leave Planet looks like a fourth, but for {4}{U} it becomes a non-legendary copy of Spock until end of turn and can attack for a second reveal.
The Spacecraft half of the list wants creatures tapped for Station charge counters (6+ for Galileo, 16+ for Enterprise) and rarely gets there; Kirk's +3/+3 is the only payoff that comes online early.

The landfall shell is lopsided: ten cards pay off a land entering (Lotus Cobra, Scute Swarm, Tireless Tracker, Amanda Grayson, Chief Kyle, M'Ress, Syndicate Liquidators, Galileo, Enterprise, Farragut) and only Exploration adds a land drop, so those ten fire once a turn. The multiplier the list is missing is land drops, not more payoffs.

Spock triggers on entering as well as attacking, and the attack trigger happens before blockers, so he does not need to connect. The precon already blinks him: Chief Kyle on landfall, Temporal Tribulation and The Guardian of Forever at instant speed (which also protects him), Balance of Terror on chapters II and III, and Colossal Clone Master enters as a non-legendary second Spock whose power is your land-name count. Janice Rand and Guardian Project pay off each re-entry, and Brainstorm, Ponder and Augur of Autumn set or show the top card. What the list lacks is a blink that needs no land drop, mana or card.

Balance of Terror's chapters trigger before combat, so blinking Spock with it trades that turn's attack trigger for an end-step enter trigger. It's a real gain on Lt. Arex, Hornet Queen, T'Pring or a land, not on Spock himself.

Interaction and engine are separate problems, so they are costed separately here: the shared four fix removal in every direction, and the six direction cards are spent on one engine rather than six unrelated upgrades.

core.name: Shared answers
core.description: Four cheap instants that go in every direction. Spot removal goes from three to six — all of it instant speed — and Counterspell stops a spell on the stack, which nothing in the list could do before.

swaps.why: One mana exiles any creature at instant speed, which is the cheapest answer in the deck. Planet Killer costs eight, must attack every combat if able, and does nothing the turn it lands.
Three mana destroys any permanent type, including the lands and enchantments the list otherwise cannot touch. Command Chair is six mana, enters tapped and only ever ramps.

Split second kills an artifact or enchantment with no response, which matters against Equipment and Rhystic-style pieces. Chief Montgomery Scott spends {6} and a tap to put one creature from your hand onto the battlefield. Giant Space Amoeba stays instead: it copies itself every time it attacks, so one flying 3/3 becomes two, then four.
Two mana stops the sweeper or the combo piece outright. Echo of Eons is a six-mana wheel that refills every opponent's hand too.

directions.name: Transporter Room
directions.pitch: The precon already makes Spock enter again — Chief Kyle, Temporal Tribulation, The Guardian of Forever and Colossal Clone Master — but each needs a land drop, mana or a card. Far Traveler gives him a free blink at every end step after he attacks, Starfield Vocalist makes every enter trigger happen twice, Gilraen and Momentary Blink blink at instant speed (which is also how this build protects him), Penance picks the card he reveals, and Hornet Queen is the free cast that gets better every time it re-enters. It folds if Spock is exiled while you're tapped out, and to effects that stop enter triggers.
directions.plays_like: Two to four Spock reveals a turn

how_to_play.summary: Attack with Spock, blink him at the end step, and let every re-entry reveal another free card.

sections.title: Turns 1–4
points: Far Traveler before Spock is the key start: from then on every attack is followed by an end-step blink, two triggers a turn for no mana.
Spend ramp on differently named lands — the free-cast ceiling is the name count, Colossal Clone Master needs six and Hornet Queen seven.
Hold Momentary Blink or {2} for Gilraen on the turn Spock lands; they are his protection as well as extra triggers.

sections.title: Turns 5–7
points: Attack with Spock every turn: the trigger fires on the attack, before blockers, and Far Traveler only blinks a creature that is tapped.
With a Spock trigger on the stack, use Penance to put your best expensive card on top. Colossal Clone Master is the best one: it enters as a second, non-legendary Spock.

With Far Traveler out, point Chief Kyle and Balance of Terror at Lt. Arex, Hornet Queen or T'Pring instead of Spock — a Spock exiled until the end step misses his own end-step blink, and Balance of Terror's chapters come before combat.
If Far Traveler is out, return Spock straight away with Gilraen: the vigilance counter from a delayed return means he no longer taps to attack.

sections.title: Closing
points: Spock and a Clone Master copy both attack, Spock blinks one of them at the end step, and Starfield Vocalist doubles that enter — three or four reveals a turn.
Order the end-step triggers so Far Traveler's blink resolves before a warped Starfield Vocalist is exiled, and the re-entry still triggers twice.
Against a board wipe, Temporal Tribulation exiles Spock and the Clone Master in response and both come back at the end step.

swaps.why: Spock gains 'at the beginning of your end step, blink a tapped creature you control', so every attack is followed by an enter trigger for no mana. It's a Background, but in the 99 it is a plain enchantment. Pike can tap two blockers for {2}, which Spock doesn't need: his trigger fires on the attack.

Every trigger caused by a permanent entering happens twice — Spock's reveal, Janice Rand's land, Guardian Project's draw and every landfall trigger in the deck. Tribble Cluster is a 1/1 that needs four combat steps to be worth a card.

Putting a card from your hand on top of your library costs no mana and works at instant speed, so before each Spock trigger resolves you choose what he reveals. Sam Kirk only investigates when an opponent casts a creature spell.

{2}, {T} blinks another creature at instant speed: the removal spell fizzles and Spock re-enters with a fresh trigger. S.S. Botany Bay is graveyard hate that needs eight charge counters before it even flies.
Two instant-speed blinks from one card, from hand and again with flashback, and each is a Spock trigger that also answers a removal spell. Merciful Mandate only untaps your team or ends one combat.

Free off Spock's trigger at seven land names, and every blink after that makes four more flying deathtouch Insects — eight with Starfield Vocalist. Scute Swarm only pays off land drops, which this direction doesn't add.

directions.name: Land Engine
directions.pitch: The stock list has the payoffs and almost none of the enablers: ten cards trigger when a land enters and Exploration is the only card that lets you play an extra one. Loot, Azusa and Wayward Swordtooth turn one land drop into three or four, Mole Man replays lands from the graveyard, and Felidar Retreat and Rampaging Baloths are the two payoffs worth adding on top of the ten already there. Every blink piece stays, so Spock's enter trigger still works on top: Colossal Clone Master copies Azusa or Spock without the legend rule, Chief Kyle blinks on each of the extra land drops, and Temporal Tribulation and Balance of Terror blink lands or Lt. Arex for more landfall triggers. The last five swaps came after the first ten were bought: Far Traveler and Momentary Blink make Spock (or Lt. Arex) enter again, Starfield Vocalist doubles every landfall and enter trigger, and two bounce lands keep the extra land drops fed.
directions.plays_like: Three or four land drops a turn, Spock blinking at every end step

how_to_play.summary: Ramp to four, then land three or four times a turn and let thirteen payoffs convert every drop into bodies.

sections.title: Turns 1–3
points: Exploration or Loot on turn two is the strongest start in the deck: every land after it is a second trigger.
Spend Farseek, Nature's Lore and Rampant Growth on differently named lands — the ramp and Spock's ceiling are the same resource.
Do not cut a land drop for a four-drop; the engine wants lands on the battlefield, not more spells in hand.

sections.title: Turns 4–6
points: With Azusa or Wayward Swordtooth online you are playing two to four lands a turn out of 40; empty your hand of lands before cracking fetches so nothing is stranded.

Simic Growth Chamber and Selesnya Sanctuary return a land to your hand: with an extra land drop left, replay it the same turn for a second trigger — a cracked fetch or a Temple (scry 1 before Spock's next reveal) is the best one to pick up.
Mole Man, Moloid Master doubles a fetch: play it, then replay the land from the graveyard for a second trigger and a second Moloid.
Colossal Clone Master copying Azusa is two more land drops — the copy isn't legendary, so both stay.
Tap two lands for mana, then cast Temporal Tribulation on them: they come back at your end step as two more landfall triggers, and flashback does it again.
Balance of Terror's chapters II and III come before combat, so blink Lt. Arex (three cards and three lands), Sun Titan or a land with them, not Spock.

sections.title: Spock's enter trigger
points: Spock is a landfall enabler too: a land he reveals goes onto the battlefield, and Janice Rand puts another one in every time he enters or attacks.

Far Traveler gives Spock an end-step blink of a tapped creature: after he attacks, blink him for a second reveal and another Janice Rand land, or blink Lt. Arex after he attacks for three more cards and three more lands.

Before Far Traveler, play your extra lands after combat: Spock attacks first, then Chief Kyle blinks him on the next land and he re-enters at the end step. Once Far Traveler is out, point Kyle at other creatures — a Spock exiled until the end step misses his own end-step blink.
When Spock enters or attacks with Janice Rand out, let Spock's reveal resolve first: Janice moves the cards above her land to the bottom, so the top card you set up would be gone.
Starfield Vocalist makes each of those enter triggers, and every landfall trigger, happen twice; warp it for {1}{U} on the turn that matters most.
Momentary Blink, The Guardian of Forever and Temporal Tribulation blink at instant speed, so hold them for the removal spell aimed at Spock.

sections.title: Closing
points: Rampaging Baloths plus two extra land drops is four 4/4 Beasts a round; the table has to answer the engine, not the individual Beasts.
Felidar Retreat is the flexible payoff — tokens when you are behind on board, counters when the ground is stable.
Spock is still a fine curve-topper and a free card every attack, but this build no longer needs him to win.

swaps.why: One extra land drop every turn, and once the land count catches up his second ability puts a creature from the top six straight onto the battlefield. Pike only taps or untaps two other creatures.
Two extra land drops turns every landfall trigger in the deck into three a turn. Tribble Cluster is a 1/1 that needs four combat steps before it is worth a card.

A third extra land drop with a 5/5 body attached — the city's blessing only gates attacking, the land drops work from turn three. Sam Kirk only investigates when an opponent casts a creature spell, one Clue at a time.

Enabler and payoff in one card: lands played from the graveyard bring fetches back for a second trigger, and every land still makes a Moloid. S.S. Botany Bay is graveyard hate that needs eight charge counters before it even flies.
With three extra land drops this makes a 2/2 per land, or grows the whole team when the board is stable. Merciful Mandate only untaps your team or ends one combat.

A 6/6 trampler that makes a 4/4 on every land drop — four Beasts a round with this shell. Christine Chapel is a four-mana 2/2 that only grows when you gain life. Balance of Terror stays: its chapters II and III blink Lt. Arex, Sun Titan or a land for more landfall.

Spock gains 'at the beginning of your end step, blink a tapped creature you control': every attack is followed by a second Spock trigger and another land from Janice Rand, for no mana. It's a Background, but in the 99 it is a plain enchantment. Uhura spends {4} and a tap every turn on a random instant or sorcery from an opponent's library.

Every trigger caused by a permanent entering happens twice: all twelve landfall payoffs, Chief Kyle, Spock's reveal and Janice Rand's land. Doubling the payoffs beats adding one more, and Syndicate Liquidators is a five-mana copy of what Amanda Grayson does for four.

Two instant-speed blinks from one card, from hand and again with flashback: each is a Spock reveal and a Janice Rand land, and each answers a removal spell aimed at him. McCoy is a five-mana 0/4 whose team-wide counter happens once.
Taps for two coloured mana and returns a land to your hand, so Azusa and Loot always have a land to replay for another trigger. Reliquary Tower is colourless and only lifts the hand-size limit.
A second bounce land: green and white instead of colourless, and another land back in hand for the extra drops. Mutavault is a colourless 2/2 the deck rarely has spare mana to animate.

directions.name: More Worlds
directions.pitch: Push the resource Spock actually counts: 43 lands and 38 different names, cutting the three colourless lands that were doing nothing in a three-colour deck. Shore Leave Planet stays, because for {4}{U} it attacks as a second Spock. Cheapest direction and the most direct upgrade to the commander, but it adds no engine.

how_to_play.summary: Trade clunky permanents for lands, then let the name count carry Spock.

sections.title: Turns 1–3
points: Play the untapped duals first (Brushland, Adarkar Wastes, Yavimaya Coast) so the name count grows without costing tempo; the pain is one life per coloured use.
Keep the four Forest, two Island, two Plains for Rampant Growth, Cultivate and Kirk to find.

sections.title: Turns 4–6
points: Every new name raises Spock's free-cast ceiling, so a six-drop on top becomes castable at six lands rather than eight.
Exploration plus 43 lands means two drops a turn is normal; do not be shy about playing lands you do not immediately need.

sections.title: Closing
points: At 38 names Spock casts almost anything on top for free; attack with him every turn to trigger it twice per round.
With spare mana, make Shore Leave Planet a copy of Spock before combat and attack with both. It stops being a land for that turn, so the name count drops by one.
You are at 43 lands with eight basics — keep two spare lands in hand for Exploration turns, and check your remaining basics before cracking Evolving Wilds.

swaps.why: An untapped green-white source with a new name for one life per coloured use. Temple of the False God is colourless and only taps once you control five lands.
Untapped white-blue fixing and a brand-new name. Mutavault is a colourless 2/2 that does not help you cast anything; this direction trades it up.
Untapped green-blue fixing and a new name. Reliquary Tower is colourless and only lifts the hand-size limit, which a 43-land deck rarely needs.
Trades a 0/6 that only taps or untaps creatures for a land that enters untapped early and adds a name. The deck goes to 43 lands, so every drop matters.
A white-blue fast land with a new name instead of a 1/1 that needs four combat steps before it is a real threat.
Green-white fixing and a new name for a 3/3 that only investigates when an opponent casts a creature spell.

recommendation: Take Land Engine (picked). After the review it cuts only cards that do nothing for either engine, so it keeps every piece that makes Spock enter again — Chief Kyle, Temporal Tribulation, The Guardian of Forever, Balance of Terror and Colossal Clone Master — and adds four land-drop enablers that keep working when Spock is answered. The five extra swaps cost under €2 and tie the two engines together: Far Traveler and Momentary Blink turn Spock's enter trigger into extra lands through Janice Rand, and Starfield Vocalist doubles both. Transporter Room is the stronger Spock-only build at about €9 if you want to push the blink side later; More Worlds is the cheapest and the safest mana base, but it adds no engine.
